title: Complete HLG-2 deterministic repository fragment discovery
context: HLG-1 is accepted and the first HLG-2 exact-source slice discovers bounded package and Git-remote candidates. The remaining discovery sources must preserve the same evidence-first candidate boundary before HLG-3 can expose bounded landscape delivery.
decision: Complete HLG-2 one deterministic source family at a time, beginning with MCP declarations, using the existing bounded issue/evidence/candidate envelope. Discovery reads one exact revision, emits content-addressed candidates without writing graph authority, rejects secret-bearing locators, and leaves identity conflicts unresolved for review. Stop before cross-repository traversal, live health, or a new delivery surface.
consequences: MCP declarations are the next source family before deployment, CI, API, event or schema breadth
Every candidate remains bound to exact file, field, revision and content evidence
Discovery never silently chooses between conflicting identities or promotes a candidate into authority
HLG-3 starts only after reviewed adoption preserves resource identity, provenance and currentness
alternatives_rejected: Begin HLG-3 delivery before repository discovery is complete enough to exercise reviewed adoption — revisit after the HLG-2 acceptance fixtures pass
Scan every manifest family in one broad heuristic pass — revisit only if incremental exact-source discovery cannot cover a required source
Resolve identity conflicts automatically from locator similarity — conflicts remain review input, not inferred authority
Move live runtime health or cross-repository traversal into Hunch — ORC owns those observations and traversal authorization

premises.claim: HLG-1 resource and relationship contracts are accepted and the first exact-source HLG-2 discovery slice exists
